rig.description: The sender's rig now, when it changed since HELLO.

game.description: The sender's fingerprint now, when its table changed since HELLO.

tableName.description: Human name of the table or ROM set.

tableHash.description: SHA-256 of the ORIGINAL .vpx (never the patched copy), or of the arcade ROM zip.

romName.description: PinMAME ROM set name (e.g. mm_109c) or arcade ROM name; null for originals.

romHash.description: SHA-256 of the ROM zip; null for originals.

physicsHash.description: Hash of the physics-relevant table settings; null when not computed.

recipeVersion.description: Castcade patch recipe version applied to this table (ADR 0004); null for arcade.

sidecarHash.description: SHA-256 of the generated sidecar .vbs; proves both players run the same patch.

emulatorVersion.description: VPX or RetroArch core version string.

ballEndReady.description: A13: whether the sender's table can report ball ends now (see `HELLO.ballEndReady`), when that changed since HELLO. Lobby only.

advisory.description: B26: after MATCH_READY only: a flag about one of the sender's own balls (see `PlayerAdvisory`). The host passes the update on to every other participant like a rig change (`from` preserved) and sends its own the same way. A peer from before B26 ignores it.

kind.description: `midnight`: Midnight Madness ran on this ball. B26.4: a fact, not a guess from the clock: the ROM's own audit of the mode went up in the sender's table NVRAM while the ball was in play.

game.description: The game of the series the ball belongs to.

ballNumber.description: The sender's ball the flag is about.

midnightMode.description: B26.4: the Midnight Madness setting on the sender's table (see `MidnightMode`), when its companion could read it, in any phase. In the lobby the host lists it in HELLO_ACK `midnightModes`; after MATCH_READY it passes the update on like a rig change. A peer from before B26.4 ignores it.

enabled.description: The adjustment reads YES (true) or NO (false) in the table's NVRAM.

adjustment.description: The adjustment as the service menu numbers and names it, e.g. `A.2 14 Special Mode`.

stream3dWaitMs.description: I11.4.9: lobby only: the sender's PC is still making its 3D connection (its VPX build has not connected to its Castcade yet, or nothing has been heard from another player's PC over the state stream's data connection), and stops waiting for it in at most this many ms; 0: settled (or given up). The host lists it in HELLO_ACK `stream3dWait` and holds a start from its table meanwhile. Absent: no change. A peer from before I11.4.9 ignores it.

stance.description: A17: the sender's choice now, Play or Watch at the next start. It changes nothing in a game that is being played.

noCopy.description: A17: true: the sender's PC has no copy of the lobby's table (`HELLO_ACK.hostGame`); false: it has.

ownGame.description: A17: true: a game the match does not own is running on the sender's table (played alone, in the lobby or as a watcher); false: it has ended.

description: client -> host in the lobby: replaces the sender's HELLO `participant.rig` and `game`; the host compares the fingerprint again and re-sends HELLO_ACK to every client; (I11.4.9) `stream3dWaitMs` says whether the sender's 3D connection is still being made. After MATCH_READY (A6.1, 2026-11-01) only `rig`, (B26) `advisory` and (B26.4) `midnightMode` count: the roster in the log stays final, and the host passes the update on to every other participant (`from` preserved) and sends its own the same way, so each Match tab and panel shows the rig each player has now. Never logged. In a lobby (A17) it counts in every phase for `rig`, `game`, `ballEndReady`, `midnightMode`, `stance`, `noCopy` and `ownGame`: the host answers with HELLO_ACK to every member, and a match's logged roster and fingerprint stay what its MATCH_READY said.
